title: prefill-ghosts-debug-diary
content:
Context:
- Symptoms: sudden 15-30% token throughput drop on a small subset of customers (~2% of requests) starting 2026-02-10 evening deploy. Latency SLO still met on p50 but p95 increased and overall cost/token rose. Not universal across models; mostly long-context chat use cases with prefill-enabled requests.

Initial hypothesis (H0): misconfigured continuous-batcher warmup/prefill logic creates 'ghost' KV snapshots that cause inefficient batching windows (smaller micro-batches + missed prefix caching) leading to lower aggregate throughput.

Quick repro attempt (local):
- Replayed sampled traffic (from dump) with same sequence length distribution and prefill flags using local runtime image built at commit 8f3a2.
- Command: 
  ./run_replay.sh --trace-file=2026-02-11-prefill-sample.json --runtime-image=local:8f3a2 --concurrency=32 --prefill=true
- Observed: average tokens/sec 12% lower vs baseline image 8c1b9 (no code change to batching code in that commit window).

Notable logs/snippets:
- runtime WARN (2026-02-10T19:24:02Z) "prefill snapshot miss: kvid=0x4f3a TTL-expired? warmup-skip=1"
- trace: "continuous-batcher: window_start=0x7f8a, window_len_ms=5ms, queued=3, scheduled=1"
- sproc: "cache_lookup latency spike 4.3ms (baseline 0.2ms)"

Commands tried while iterating:
- Toggle prefill off in replay: --prefill=false => throughput returns to baseline. Suggests prefill path implicated.
- Force batch window > 10ms: RUNTIME_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=12 => throughput recovers ~+8% but latency p50 slightly higher.
- Patch: add jitter to prefill cache invalidation to avoid synchronized TTL expirations (small experiment) => inconsistent improvement, sometimes helps.

Telemetry slices observed:
- Affected requests: has_prefill=true AND sequence_len>1024 AND origin=hosted-api.us-east-1
- Correlation: high KV cache churn + small batching windows (<=6ms) leads to runaway scheduling overhead.
- Environmental: spikes follow scheduled index-rotation Cron job at ~19:00 UTC (coincidence?).

Hypotheses considered:
- H1: Prefill TTLs aligned across workers cause synchronized cache invalidations => many requests fall back to warmup/prefill, overwhelming batcher and causing smaller windows.
- H2: A change in kernel selection heuristics (fallback to slower kernels during prefill) leads to per-token slowdown only when prefill path used. (less likely: profiling shows kernel times unchanged).
- H3: Autoscaler briefly reduces worker count due to mis-labeled health probes concurrent with prefill churn, amplifying per-worker load.

Micro experiments & results summary:
- Experiment A: Staggered prefill TTLs across process start times (implemented via RAND(TTL%10)) -> reduces 95th p95 overflows in local runs but not consistent in prod canary.
- Experiment B: Increase batch window to 12ms globally for affected pool -> recovers throughput but increases tail latency for short-response requests. Good for Dedicated but bad for low-latency Hosted tier.
- Experiment C: Short-circuit prefill path for 'trusted' customers -> solved for those customers but not general solution.

Runtime traces (short):
- request 0xabc: prefill_lookup -> miss -> enqueue warmup -> batcher scheduled immediately (window=3ms) -> execution -> finish. Several concurrent warmups cause head-of-queue starvation for normal requests.

Open debug actions (next steps):
1) Add finer telemetry: emit event on prefill-miss with worker_id, process_uptime, TTL-version to see alignment across processes. (Jonah)
2) Run controlled canary with staggered TTL algorithm in us-east-1 busy pool for 3 hours, watch cost and p95 (Evan).
3) Add a guarding heuristic in batcher: if >N warmup tasks queued, temporarily increase batch window for that pool category. Implement as quick kill-switch. (Priya)
4) Validate autoscaler logs around 2026-02-10 19:00 UTC for scale-down events (SRE).

Notes to self / friction points:
- Drive replay fidelity: replay doesn't perfectly match real KV hotness patterns; need a small in-situ canary.
- Be careful: increasing batch window globally affects latency-sensitive users; prefer pool-targeted fixes.
- Keep product informed: this could be an avoidable regression if prefill TTL defaults changed in the config rollout.

Scratch ideas for permanent fixes:
- Make prefill TTL randomized per-process on startup (small entropy) + telemetry to measure alignment.
- Batcher-level adaptive window: base on queued warmup ratio. If warmup_ratio > 0.2, bias window + jitter.
- Prefill backoff: after X consecutive misses for a customer session, avoid warmup prefill for short window (fallback to on-demand).

Questions to raise in sync:
- Was there a config rollout around 2026-02-10 that changed prefill TTLs or cache eviction behavior? (Product infra)
- Can we ship a tactical kill-switch (env var) to disable prefill on affected visible pools quickly?

Quick links:
- replay script: ./tools/replay/README.md
- telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.de/d/qzK-prefill-heatmap

Timestamped log of small runs (local):
- 2026-02-16 11:04: baseline image 8c1b9: tokens/sec 2150
- 2026-02-16 11:18: suspect image 8f3a2: tokens/sec 1860 (–13%)
- 2026-02-17 09:21: TTL-jitter build: tokens/sec 2025 (–5%), unstable

Status: still investigating; leaning towards H1 (synchronized TTL/cache churn) + batcher window interaction. Will run targeted canary + implement temporary batcher guard.
summary: investigation notes for a throughput regression tied to prefill/prefill-miss behavior causing small batching windows and KV cache churn
